researcher_notes: Opus full-redo pass. SCOPE OF THIS FILE: the EIGHT single-model datasheets in the VisionNav group (nine files, since `1785316235.pdf` has a byte-identical duplicate `1785316235-2.pdf`, md5 2099dccf6ddf373870e63859b2599bbd). All filenames are bare numeric epochs with no model name — attribution is from p.1 of each document. Two files are DELIBERATELY NOT covered here and remain unprocessed: `1657089341.pdf` (18 pp full-range catalog, older -01/-07 generation) and `1685356775.pdf` (14 pp, almost entirely image-only — 56–394 characters of extractable text per page — so it needs image-based reading). They are a separate unit of work; see `outstanding` at the end. TWO DOCUMENT GENERATIONS are present in this corpus and they disagree, which matters for every conflict below: the older 'AUTOMATE YOUR INTRALOGISTICS' sheets (2023, model codes with -01/-07/(V)/(L) suffixes) and the newer 'FULL SPECTRUM LOGISTICS AUTOMATION' sheets (no suffix, imperial columns, B56.5 badge). Where both exist for one model, both are cited. Nothing written to Airtable.

company_wide_context.applies_to: all base models of this company — WITH the two stated exceptions
company_wide_context.notes: MUST be fanned out per base model, and the two exceptions must be honoured — VNK15 is the odd one out on both environmental fields (0 °C not −5 °C, 90 % not 95 %). AP0 GAP, and it is a strong one for this supplier: every VisionNav sheet publishes a **ground flatness** requirement in mm/m² — ±5 mm/m² (VNQ50, VNKQ20, and the older T-series), ±10 mm/m² (VNE20, VNE40), **3 mm/m² (VNK15)** — plus a **max. gap width** (30–50 mm) and a **max. obstacle/step height** (5–50 mm). `floor_flatness_req`'s allowed values are the categorical ['Standard (FM2)','High (FM1)','Very High (F-number)','None stated'], which cannot express a millimetre figure at all. This is the 9th+ instance of the gap and VisionNav quantifies it more consistently than any other supplier in the corpus — worth citing when the field is revised. Also unstorable across the whole range: 'Localization/Positioning Precision' (±10 mm/±0.5° to ±15 mm/±1°) and, more importantly, **'Loading Adaptability' / 'Pick-up Adaptability' ±100 mm/±10°** — how badly a pallet may be misplaced and still be picked up automatically, which is exactly the brownfield question a buyer asks and maps to none of AP0's `pick_req_accuracy_*` fields (those describe the required accuracy, not the tolerated error).

max_payload.source: p.3 row 9, 'Rated Load Capacity **2800kg (4000mm)** | 6180 lb (157 in)' — and the imperial column carries the derating parenthetical too, '(157 in)' = 4000 mm, so this is not a stray annotation
max_payload.note: K.O. field, and **the most striking payload-derating artefact found in the whole redo**: the manufacturer prints the derated capacity *as the rated capacity*, with the lift height it applies at in brackets, in both metric and imperial. The model designation VNE40 implies 4000 kg (consistent with VNE20/30/35 = 2000/3000/3500 kg), so the truck presumably lifts 4000 kg at low height and only 2800 kg at 4 m. AP0 stores one `max_payload` and cannot express the pair. **NOT resolvable from this document** — it does not print the low-height rating. Recommend asking VisionNav for the full load chart before touching the value; entering 4000 overstates high-lift capability and entering 2800 understates ground-level capability.

This sheet says the VNE40 reaches 7000 mm. Combined with the payload conflict above, the VNE40 row is the least reliable in the VisionNav set.

towing_capacity.note: K.O. field, and the largest single numeric error found in this redo — the DB overstates towing capacity by 4×. The datasheet is unambiguous and prints its own imperial conversion (5000 kg = 11023.1 lb, correct to 0.01 %). Unit forensics on the stored 19958 per the false-positive checklist: it is not 5000 kg in lb (11023), not 5000 lb in kg (2268), and not a ×2/×4 of any printed figure — 19958 lb would be 9053 kg and 19958 kg would be 44 000 lb, neither of which appears anywhere. **No unit explanation exists; it looks like a transcription error, not a conversion artefact.** The vehicle weighs 1080 kg (row 4), so a ~20 t rated draw is also physically implausible for it.

max_payload_wrong_field.datasheet: 5000 kg is the TRACTION capacity, not a payload
max_payload_wrong_field.source: p.3 row 5, 'Rated **Traction** Capacity 5000kg'. The datasheet publishes no payload row at all — this is a tow tractor with a tow pin (row 6, 'Tow Pin Height 300mm'), not a load carrier.
max_payload_wrong_field.note: SEMANTIC error rather than a numeric one, and the two conflicts on this row are almost certainly the same mistake seen twice: the real 5000 kg traction figure landed in `max_payload` and something else landed in `towing_capacity`. **The correct record is `towing_capacity = 5000` and `max_payload = NULL`.** Not applied. This matters because a Tugger AGV with a non-null `max_payload` will be scored against payload requirements it was never designed to meet.

products.notes: CONFIRMS max_payload=1500 (p.3 row 9, 'Rated Load Capacity 1500kg | 3306.93lb'), lift 60 mm (row 7 — the DB stores this in the Forklift-scope `lifting_height` field on a Mobile AMR row; the AMR-scope field is `lift_height`. Wrong-scope, flag only), max_speed=1.8 (row 14, 'Max Forward Speed（Loaded/Empty） 1.5m/s, **1.8m/s**' — the DB's 1.8 is the UNLADEN figure; the laden figure is 1.5, and a reviewer standardising on laden speeds should change it). **`min_turning_radius` DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL, and the reasoning is worth recording because this model has been ambiguous across three sessions:** the p.2 dimension drawing carries '**φ1200**' — the φ symbol means DIAMETER — alongside 1150, 620 and 280. A prior session found the same figure labelled 'Min Truning Diameter 1200mm' [sic] on another VisionNav sheet. Applying the footprint-diagonal check that settled Magazino SOTO: a 1150 × 820 mm body rotating about its centroid sweeps a circle of diameter √(1150²+820²) ≈ 1412 mm, which is LARGER than 1200 mm. So φ1200 cannot be the swept circle of the whole vehicle — it is more likely the diameter of the rotating lift platform itself. Neither 1200 nor 600 is safe to write into `min_turning_radius`. **This is now a settled negative case: do not map VNK15's 1200 mm figure, and record why.** The DB row also carries `humidity_control_capable = 1`, a field that does not exist in `config/fields.json` under any AGV scope (same observation as Omron LD-130CT) — worth a schema audit. Unstorable: weight 180 kg; 'Min Traveling Aisle Width ＞200mm' (row 20 — a remarkable figure, and AMR scope has no aisle field anyway, 14th+ instance); ground flatness 3 mm/m² (the tightest floor requirement of any VisionNav model); max obstacle height 5 mm; 'Average Turning Time 3s' / 'Average Lifting Time 4s' (cycle-time components with no AP0 field). `rotation_capable` NOT set: nothing here describes turning a carried rack to face a picker.

field_sources.min_turning_radius: p.3 row 10, 'Min. Turning Radius 1000mm | 39.37in' — explicit English 'Radius' label, and `min_turning_radius` IS the AMR-scope field, so scope and value agree. Sanity check: a 2400 × 500 mm body has a circumscribed-circle radius of √(2400²+500²)/2 ≈ 1226 mm, so a 1000 mm turning radius is only achievable because the vehicle is bidirectional and does not need to swing its full length — plausible but worth the reviewer's eye.

max_payload.datasheet: 2000 kg is the TRACTION capacity, not a payload
max_payload.source: p.3 row 5, 'Rated **Traction** Capacity 2000kg | 4409lb'; row 6, 'Tow Pin Height 230-270mm'; row 9, 'Drive Direction Bidirectional Travel'
max_payload.note: SEMANTIC conflict, the same shape as VNQ50 above — and the second instance in this one supplier. This vehicle has a tow pin and a traction rating, and the datasheet publishes NO payload row. Storing 2000 in `max_payload` makes it look like a 2 t load carrier, which will win payload-based matches it cannot serve. Correct record: the 2000 belongs in a towing field.

product_type.source: p.1, 'VNKQ20 | **TUNNELLING AMR**'; p.3 row 5 'Rated Traction Capacity', row 6 'Tow Pin Height 230-270mm'
product_type.note: K.O.-level classification, flagged rather than changed. The manufacturer's own label says AMR, but the machine's defining features are a tow pin and a traction rating with no payload — the AP0 definition of a tugger. Note the DB's sibling VNQ50, a functionally similar tow unit, IS classified Tugger AGV. Consistency argues for Tugger; the manufacturer's wording argues for AMR. **This is exactly the kind of call this agent should not make alone** — and it has a knock-on effect, because the scope decides whether `towing_capacity`/`coupling_type` (Tugger) or `min_ground_clearance`/`min_turning_radius` (AMR) are even available fields for it. The values proposed above assume the DB's current AMR classification; if it is reclassified, `min_ground_clearance` and `min_turning_radius` must be dropped and `towing_capacity = 2000` added.

products.notes: CONFIRMS max_speed=1.5 in neither direction, which is worth noting: this sheet's speed rows give only 'Max Turning Forward Speed (Loaded,Empty) 0.3m/s,0.6m/s' (row 16) — there is no straight-line max-speed row at all in the extracted table, so the DB's stored 1.5 m/s is unverified by this document. `omnidirectional_movement` deliberately NOT set despite row 9's 'Bidirectional Travel' — bidirectional is not omnidirectional, a distinction already drawn for Kivnon K11 earlier in this session. Placing it in context: DB VNR16 holds 1600 kg / 5500 mm / 3250 mm aisle and VNR20 holds 2000 kg / 7000 mm / 3300 mm aisle, so a 1400 kg model reaching **8555 mm** is the tallest of the three despite being the lightest — which is exactly the payload-vs-lift-height trade-off pattern, this time visible across sibling models rather than within one. **That in turn casts doubt on the VNR16 and VNR20 lift heights**, since a lighter truck out-reaching both heavier ones by 1.5–3 m is unusual; a reviewer should re-check those two rows against their own datasheets (not present in this corpus). 6 pages; only p.1's headline block was extracted for the K.O. fields. `navigation_type` includes 'Vision' on the strength of 'Vision-based or 3D SLAM' — note the 'or': the two are alternative builds, not a combined stack, which AP0's multi-select cannot express.

files_left_in_Analysed: 1657089341.pdf — 18-page full-range product catalog, older -01/-07 generation, text-extractable. Sampled but NOT fully processed in this session. It contains per-model spec blocks for at least the T series (VNT20(V)-01: 2000 kg, 125 mm lift, 2800 mm min stacking aisle, 2300 mm min turning aisle, 2.0 m/s, vision-based navigation, −5 to 45 °C) and the E series (VNE20（VL）-07: 3300 kg weight, 3397×1250×2042 mm, 2000 kg, 3000 mm lift, 3900 mm aisle, 2.0 m/s), plus a systems/architecture section (p.3: RCS 'visualized intelligent scheduling system for up to **150 AGVs**' — a `max_fleet_size` value, and 'BrightEye System' deep-learning rack-occupancy detection). **Its main value is as the older-generation reference for models whose DB rows may predate the newer sheets, and for `max_fleet_size` which no other VisionNav file states.**
